title: LORE Crypto History — 250 events / Season One 100

scope_approval.basis: User liked the proposed timeline approach and asked to confirm the timeline and 100 cards. This approves preparation and scope, not unseen individual artwork or final copy.

coverage.current_year_policy: 2026 is a provisional-perspective supporting chapter; no 2026 artwork is assigned in this selection.

selection_method: Manual editorial curation from year-shard research, balancing historical significance, narrative clarity, visual potential and coverage. No numerical ranking of the full discovery archive was performed.

provenance.canonical_year_files_untouched_except: 2025.json receives two new sourced entries; all other year research remains unchanged.
provenance.note: Year and month precision, historical legal qualifiers, announcement-versus-event distinctions and unresolved evidence limits are retained.

date_policy: Use the source-established precision. Dates retain source calendar conventions; UTC is explicit when known. A year-only or month-only date is never expanded to a fabricated day. Sort undated-within-year/month items after precisely dated items in that period.
approval_policy: Scope, event selection, final wording, visual approval and print release are separate. Existing 11 approvals persist; 89 proposed events are not 89 approved artworks. Existing production holds persist.

display.featured_entries: 100 card moments, showing exact approved art where available
display.qr_rule: Physical card QR should resolve to its event page with a link back to the timeline; current demo QR values are not changed by this selection.
display.delivery: Data and editorial review documents only; no website deployment or image generation in this milestone.

events.title: Diffie and Hellman publish foundational public-key cryptography work
events.summary: Diffie and Hellman published New Directions in Cryptography, introducing the public-key cryptography framework and digital-signature concept to the open literature.
events.historical_significance: Foundational cryptographic infrastructure later used by digital-cash systems and cryptocurrencies.

source_provenance.original_title: Diffie and Hellman publish foundational public-key cryptography work

events.title: David Chaum proposes cryptographic digital cash
events.summary: Chaum presented Blind Signatures for Untraceable Payments at CRYPTO '82, a direct foundation for privacy-preserving electronic cash.
events.historical_significance: One of the clearest technical ancestors of cryptocurrency-era digital cash.

source_provenance.original_title: David Chaum proposes cryptographic digital cash

events.title: The Crypto Anarchist Manifesto circulates
events.summary: Timothy May stated that The Crypto Anarchist Manifesto dated to mid-1988 and was distributed at Crypto '88; he posted it electronically to the Cypherpunks list in November 1992.
events.historical_significance: It articulated the political and social vision that influenced later cypherpunk digital-money work.

source_provenance.original_title: The Crypto Anarchist Manifesto circulates

events.title: DigiCash is founded

events.title: Cypherpunks mailing list emerges
events.summary: Eric Hughes sent the welcome message establishing the Cypherpunks mailing list infrastructure on toad.com.

events.title: A Cypherpunk's Manifesto

events.title: US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve established
events.summary: A US executive order established a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve capitalized initially with finally forfeited government BTC and directed that Bitcoin deposited into the reserve not be sold.
events.historical_significance: The policy transformed confiscated Bitcoin from an asset normally disposed of by government into a formally designated reserve category.

events.title: The US GENIUS Act is signed into law
events.summary: The US President signed S. 1582, the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act), into law.
events.historical_significance: The law created a federal statutory framework for payment stablecoins, marking a major shift from agency-led enforcement and state-by-state rules toward national legislation.

events.title: Ethereum Fusaka upgrade
events.summary: Ethereum activated the Fulu-Osaka (Fusaka) upgrade at epoch 411,392.
events.historical_significance: Fusaka advanced Ethereum's data-availability and Layer-2 scaling roadmap while also increasing Layer-1 performance capacity.

source_provenance.original_title: Ethereum Fusaka upgrade

events.title: Ethereum's second Fusaka BPO fork raises blob capacity again
events.summary: The second Blob Parameter Only fork following Fusaka activated on 7 January 2026, raising Ethereum's per-block blob target to 14 and maximum to 21.
events.historical_significance: It extended Fusaka's PeerDAS scaling plan by increasing rollup data capacity without waiting for another full network upgrade.

events.title: SEC and CFTC issue joint crypto-asset legal interpretation
events.summary: The SEC issued an interpretation clarifying how federal securities laws apply to certain crypto assets and transactions, with the CFTC joining to state it would administer the Commodity Exchange Act consistently with the interpretation.
events.historical_significance: The joint action was a major attempt by the two principal US market regulators to provide a common federal framework for classifying and treating crypto activity.

events.summary: The CFTC approved KalshiEX's BTCPERP, a perpetual futures contract referencing the spot price of Bitcoin.
events.historical_significance: The approval brought a crypto-native perpetual-contract structure into a CFTC-regulated US exchange framework.

events.summary: The SEC proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, a tailored securities-offering regime for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets, including new registration exemptions and a conditional safe harbor.
events.historical_significance: If adopted, the proposal could materially reshape how some crypto-related offerings access US capital markets; as of September 2026 it remains a proposal, not a final rule.

events.summary: BitMEX announced on 23 July that it would wind down following a strategic review, and all exchange trading ceased at 04:00 UTC on 23 September 2026.
events.historical_significance: The closure ended the exchange most closely associated with popularizing the crypto perpetual swap and 100x leverage during the industry's early derivatives era.
